title: Data Science
blurb: The maths behind models and the full arc of a data science project, from framing to proven impact.

quiz.question: Why standardise features before gradient descent?
options: It makes the loss surface well-conditioned so gradient descent converges faster and more stably
quiz.explanation: Features on very different scales create elongated loss surfaces and zig-zagging updates.

quiz.question: A test is 95% sensitive with a 2% false-positive rate; prevalence is 0.5%. Roughly what share of positives are true?
Minimising cross-entropy loss in logistic regression is equivalent to…
options: Maximising the Bernoulli likelihood of the labels
quiz.explanation: Cross-entropy is the negative log-likelihood of a Bernoulli model.

quiz.question: For a churn model built from weekly snapshots, how should you split data?
options: By time: train on earlier snapshots, test on later ones
quiz.explanation: Time-based splits mimic deployment and prevent future information leaking into training.

quiz.question: The churn model has high AUC but the retention campaign showed no gain. Most likely reason?
options: Predicting churn is not predicting who responds to the offer (uplift)
The model was overfit to the test set
quiz.explanation: Target persuadable customers using experiments and uplift modelling.

problems.title: Frame a churn project
problems.prompt: Turn "build a churn model" into a well-framed project.
problems.solution: Define the decision (who gets which offer under a budget), a precise churn label and observation window, the success metric (incremental net revenue via A/B test), constraints (refresh cadence, explainability, no sensitive attributes), and a baseline rule to beat.
